claim: Cell fusion between bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells and cancer cells can generate hybrid cells with enhanced stemness and metastatic capabilities.

evidence.quote: Taken together, our results suggested that cell fusion between lung cancer cells and MSCs offered enhanced metastatic capacity and characteristics of cancer stem cell by undergoing EMT.
evidence.note: MSC-lung cancer hybrids show enhanced metastatic capacity and cancer stem cell characteristics; not bone-marrow specific. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Bone marrow-derived MSCs and generic cancer cells not stated; only lung cancer cell-MSC fusion.

evidence.quote: Cell fusion is shown to take part in the formation of CS/ICs, i.e. fusion between mesenchymal stem cell and cancer cell. In a previous paper, we described that fusion leads to hybrids with metastatic capacity.
evidence.note: MSC-cancer cell fusion contributes to cancer stem/initiating cells and yields hybrids with metastatic capacity. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Bone marrow-derived origin and enhanced stemness not stated.

claim: CRISPR-based epigenome editing tools including dCas9 fused to epigenetic modifying enzymes enable precise rewriting of epigenetic marks at specific genomic loci.

evidence.quote: Here, we present CRISPRoff-a programmable epigenetic memory writer consisting of a single dead Cas9 fusion protein that establishes DNA methylation and repressive histone modifications.
evidence.note: dCas9 fusion writes DNA methylation and repressive histone marks. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Precise rewriting at specific loci and general dCas9-epigenetic enzyme tools not stated.

evidence.quote: Targeted DNA cleavage techniques such as CRISPR-Cas9 system, CRISPR-dCas9 complexes, transcription activator-like effector nucleases (TALENs) and zinc-finger nucleases (ZFNs) have been exploited as targeted DNA recognition or anchoring platforms, fused with epigenetic writer or eraser proteins and delivered by transfection or transduction methods.
evidence.note: Notes dCas9 complexes fused with epigenetic writer/eraser proteins; no statement of altered marks at loci.

claim: CRISPR-based functional screens enable systematic interrogation of genes and pathways required for CSC maintenance, therapeutic resistance, and metastatic capacity.

evidence.quote: Here, we develop a CRISPR screen based on our engineered live-cell CTCF-cohesin contact reporters to identify regulators of chromatin loops. Our findings reveal that tousled-like kinase 2 (TLK2) functions as a key regulator of chromatin loop formation during the cancer stemness transition.
evidence.note: CRISPR screen identified TLK2 for cancer stemness plasticity; metastasis effect appears in later sentences, not resistance.

evidence.quote: Using CRISPR-Cas9 approaches in patient-derived GBM stem cells (GSCs) to interrogate function of the coding genome, we identify actionable pathways responsible for growth, which reveal the gene-essential circuitry of GBM stemness and proliferation.
evidence.note: CRISPR screens in GBM stem cells reveal growth/stemness pathways; metastasis not mentioned.

claim: MSC-loaded oncolytic adenoviruses produce substantial tumor shrinkage in preclinical models, and clinical translation is ongoing.

evidence.quote: Administration of OV-loaded MSCs with radiotherapy to mice bearing brainstem DIPG xenografts results in more prolonged survival relative to that conferred by either therapy alone (P < 0.01).
evidence.note: MSC-delivered oncolytic virus prolongs survival in DIPG xenograft mice; tumor size not reported; virus is not specified as adenovirus-only.

claim: Switchable CAR systems provide temporal control over therapeutic activity, enabling dose titration and emergency shutdown if severe toxicity occurs.

evidence.quote: The dose of dasatinib can be titrated to achieve partial or complete inhibition of CAR T cell function.
evidence.note: Dose titration gives partial or complete inhibition of CAR T function with a pharmacologic switch. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Switchable CAR temporal control and emergency shutdown for toxicity not stated; only dasatinib titration.

evidence.quote: In vivo, ON-switch split CARs demonstrated lenalidomide-dependent antitumor activity, and OFF-switch degradable CARs were depleted by drug treatment to limit inflammatory cytokine production while retaining antitumor efficacy.
evidence.note: Drug-controlled OFF-switch CARs limit cytokine production; no explicit emergency-shutdown or dose-titration statement.

claim: Synthetic Notch receptors enable engineered cells to sense tumor microenvironmental cues and activate customized therapeutic programs in response.

evidence.quote: To overcome suppression, we engineered circuits in which tumor-specific synNotch receptors locally induce production of the cytokine IL-2.
evidence.note: Tumor-specific synNotch receptors locally induce IL-2 production in engineered T cells. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Sensing multiple microenvironmental cues and customized programs; only IL-2 induction circuits.

evidence.quote: A synNotch receptor that recognizes a specific priming antigen, such as the heterogeneous but tumor-specific glioblastoma neoantigen epidermal growth factor receptor splice variant III (EGFRvIII) or the central nervous system (CNS) tissue-specific antigen myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG), can be used to locally induce expression of a CAR.
evidence.note: synNotch senses a priming antigen and induces CAR; antigen sensing rather than broader microenvironment cues.

claim: Cancer cells can lose tumor-associated antigens through genetic mutations, deletions, or epigenetic silencing, allowing antigen-loss variants to escape recognition by tumor-specific T cells.

evidence.quote: Transfection of each melanoma cell line with a wild-type beta2m gene restored HLA class I antigen expression and, in Me18105 cells, recognition by Melan-A/MART-1-specific, HLA-A2-restricted cytotoxic T lymphocytes.
evidence.note: beta2m mutations cause HLA class I loss; restoring it restores CTL recognition. Concerns HLA, not tumor-associated antigens.

claim: Cancer cells reduce expression of CXCR3 chemokine ligands (CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11), which are critical for recruiting CD8+ T cells to tumor sites.

evidence.quote: Mechanistic studies reveal that tumor cell-intrinsic MBTPS1 competes with USP13 for binding to STAT1, thereby disrupting the USP13-dependent deubiquitination-mediated STAT1 stabilization. The upregulated STAT1-transcribed chemokines including CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11, promote CXCR3+CD8+ T cell infiltration.
evidence.note: Tumor-cell MBTPS1 limits STAT1-driven CXCL9/10/11, which promote CXCR3+CD8+ T cell infiltration; reduction by cancer cells is implied, not stated generally.

evidence.quote: The CXCR3 ligands, CXCL9 and CXCL10, were significantly upregulated following dual PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade and both CD8+ T-cell infiltration and therapeutic efficacy were CXCR3 dependent.
evidence.note: CXCR3 ligands drive CD8+ T-cell infiltration after checkpoint blockade; no statement that cancer cells reduce them.

claim: Even though the immune defense system possesses multiple mechanisms for eliminating malignant cells, tumors develop an immunosuppressive microenvironment favorable to their progression through recruitment and education of immunosuppressive myeloid populations.

evidence.quote: Myeloid cells are pivotal within the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. The accumulation of tumour-modified myeloid cells derived from monocytes or neutrophils - termed 'myeloid-derived suppressor cells' - and tumour-associated macrophages is associated with poor outcome and resistance to treatments such as chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors.
evidence.note: Tumour-modified myeloid cells accumulate and are pivotal in the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Recruitment and education of myeloid cells and multiple elimination mechanisms not stated; only association with poor outcome.

evidence.quote: Mechanistically, NNMT-induced H3K27me3 hypomethylation drives complement secretion from CAFs, attracting immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) to the tumour.
evidence.note: Tumour-associated fibroblasts attract immunosuppressive MDSCs to tumours via complement secretion (recruitment). Strict re-read: the quote does not state Recruitment and education of myeloid cells in general; quote is NNMT/CAF/MDSC mechanism.

claim: Exhausted T cells gradually lose their capacity for robust cytokine production, proliferation, and cytotoxic functions, yet importantly, they are not completely inert—they retain some residual function that contributes to partial tumor control.

evidence.quote: Tpex cells, critically regulated by zinc finger and BTB domain containing 27 (Zbtb27)/Bcl6 transcription factor, could be reinvigorated during immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy, while Ttex cells, characterized by stronger proliferation and cytotoxicity, play an indispensable role in tumor control.
evidence.note: Terminally exhausted cells described with stronger proliferation and cytotoxicity and a role in tumor control; conflicts with 'lose' framing.

evidence.quote: Our results indicate that increasing the number of cytotoxic Tim-3+CD8+ T cells can promote effective anti-tumor immunity
evidence.note: Terminally exhausted Tim-3+ cells are cytotoxic and can promote anti-tumor immunity; no statement of gradual loss.

claim: Experiments in animals have, however, provided evidence for immune responses to tumors and have shown that T cells are a critical mediator of tumor immunity.

evidence.quote: Here, we show that CD8+ T cells deficient in both PD-1 and LAG-3, in contrast to CD8+ T cells lacking either receptor, mediate enhanced tumor clearance and long-term survival in mouse models of melanoma.
evidence.note: In mouse melanoma models, engineered CD8+ T cells mediate tumor clearance and survival. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Only PD-1/LAG-3 deficient CD8 T cells in mouse melanoma; T cells as critical mediator not stated.

evidence.quote: We demonstrated that Stub1 knockout CD8+ T cells effectively control tumor growth across multiple murine models.
evidence.note: In murine models CD8+ T cells control tumor growth; shows T-cell role, not 'critical' or evidence of tumor immunity generally.

claim: Genetic alterations affecting PD-L1 expression are frequent in hematological malignancies, and various post-translational modifications—including phosphorylation and N-glycosylation—stabilize PD-L1 at the cell surface, enhancing its immunosuppressive capacity.

evidence.quote: Moreover, TMUB1 enhances PD-L1 N-glycosylation and stability by recruiting STT3A, thereby promoting PD-L1 maturation and tumor immune evasion.
evidence.note: N-glycosylation stabilizes PD-L1 and promotes immune evasion; nothing on phosphorylation or surface location.

evidence.quote: S195 phosphorylation induces abnormal PD-L1 glycosylation, resulting in its ER accumulation and ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD).
evidence.note: S195 phosphorylation of PD-L1 leads to degradation, opposite to claim for phosphorylation.

claim: Loss and Downregulation of MHC Class I Expression: One of the most fundamental mechanisms of immune evasion involves alterations in major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecule expression.

evidence.quote: MHC I molecules are not essential for cell survival and therefore one mechanism by which cancers can evade immune control is by losing MHC I antigen presentation machinery (APM).
evidence.note: Losing MHC I antigen presentation machinery is a mechanism by which cancers evade immune control. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Quote says 'one mechanism', not 'one of the most fundamental' mechanisms of immune evasion.

evidence.quote: Loss of MHC class I (MHC-I) antigen presentation in cancer cells can elicit immunotherapy resistance.
evidence.note: Loss of MHC-I antigen presentation in cancer cells can elicit immunotherapy resistance. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Claim of one of most fundamental immune evasion mechanisms; downregulation; quote only MHC-I loss yields immunotherapy resistance.

claim: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), regulatory T cells, and tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) represent well-characterized players in tumor-induced immune suppression.

evidence.quote: Tumor-associated macrophages, resident microglia, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, neutrophils, regulatory T cells, and glioma-derived extracellular vesicles collectively establish a suppressive niche through cytokine signaling, metabolic restriction, checkpoint ligand expression, impaired phagocytosis, and extracellular matrix remodeling.
evidence.note: TAMs, MDSCs and Tregs together establish a suppressive niche in glioblastoma. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Quote is specific to glioma; not general well-characterized players in tumor-induced immune suppression.

evidence.quote: Angiogenesis factors drive immune suppression by directly suppressing the antigen-presenting cells as well as immune effector cells or through augmenting the effect of regulatory T cells (Treg), myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC), and tumor-associated macrophages (TAM).
evidence.note: Treg, MDSC and TAM mediate tumor immune suppression driven by angiogenesis factors. Strict re-read: the quote does not state 'Well-characterized players' not stated; quote says angiogenesis factors augment these cells.

claim: T-cell exhaustion represents a state of progressive T-cell dysfunction that arises during chronic antigen stimulation in the context of cancer and chronic infections.

evidence.quote: 'T cell exhaustion' is a broad term that has been used to describe the response of T cells to chronic antigen stimulation, first in the setting of chronic viral infection but more recently in response to tumours.
evidence.note: Defines exhaustion as T-cell response to chronic antigen stimulation, in chronic viral infection and tumours. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Progressive T-cell dysfunction not stated; quote is a broad-term definition.

evidence.quote: However, cancer is associated with T cell exhaustion, a hypofunctional state characterized by progressive loss of T cell effector functions and self-renewal capacity.
evidence.note: Exhaustion in cancer as hypofunction with progressive loss of effector function; chronic infection not mentioned.

claim: TAMs, which often constitute a substantial fraction of the tumor mass, generally promote tumor progression by supporting angiogenesis, tissue invasion, and metastasis.

evidence.quote: M2-polarized macrophages, commonly deemed tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), are contributors to many pro-tumorigenic outcomes in cancer through angiogenic and lymphangiogenic regulation, immune suppression, hypoxia induction, tumor cell proliferation, and metastasis.
evidence.note: M2-polarized TAMs promote angiogenesis, metastasis and progression; only the M2 subset, no tumor-mass fraction.

evidence.quote: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are among the most abundant immune cells infiltrating the TME and are present at all stages of liver cancer progression,
evidence.note: TAMs are among the most abundant infiltrating immune cells in liver cancer; no tumor-mass fraction given.

claim: The incidence of the common tumors in mice that lack lymphocytes is little different from their incidence in mice with normal immune systems; the same is true for humans deficient in T cells.

evidence.quote: The appearance of the nude mouse, athymic, and yet free of spontaneous tumors, led to a new paradigm, the network theory proposed by Jerne.
evidence.note: Athymic nude mice are described as free of spontaneous tumors; supports claim for T-cell-deficient mice only, no human data.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, severe combined immunodeficient mice are prone to spontaneous tumor development and therefore serve as experimental models.
evidence.note: Says immunodeficient mice are prone to spontaneous tumors, in a lymphoid-malignancy context; conflicts with claim, not common tumors.

claim: The molecular basis of T-cell exhaustion involves persistent antigen exposure driving hyperactivation of T cells, which ultimately leads to sustained co-expression of multiple inhibitory receptors including PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3, 2B4, CD160, and TIGIT.

evidence.quote: Upon induction of T cell exhaustion in response to persistent antigen, prominently in the anti-tumor immune response, many are expressed simultaneously. Key inhibitory receptors are CTLA-4, PD-1, LAG3, TIM3 and TIGIT, as investigated here.
evidence.note: Persistent antigen induces exhaustion with simultaneous inhibitory receptors, naming CTLA-4, PD-1, LAG3, TIM3, TIGIT; 2B4/CD160 not named. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Hyperactivation, 2B4 and CD160 not stated; quote lists different receptor set.

evidence.quote: Tox-deleted TST cells did not upregulate genes for inhibitory receptors (such as Pdcd1, Entpd1, Havcr2, Cd244 and Tigit)
evidence.note: Names exhaustion-associated inhibitory receptor genes including Cd244 (2B4) and Tigit; does not describe co-expression or hyperactivation.

claim: The transcriptional regulation of exhaustion is governed by specific transcription factors—including NFAT, TOX, NR4A1, and IRF4—that establish and maintain the exhausted state.

evidence.quote: Here we demonstrate that the transcription factor NFAT controls the program of T cell exhaustion.
evidence.note: NFAT controls the exhaustion program; TOX, NR4A1 and IRF4 not addressed in this passage.

evidence.quote: TOX is largely dispensable for the formation of Teff and Tmem cells, but it is critical for exhaustion: in the absence of TOX, Tex cells do not form. TOX is induced by calcineurin and NFAT2,
evidence.note: TOX is critical for exhaustion and induced by NFAT2; NR4A1 and IRF4 not mentioned.

claim: Treg cells suppress effector T-cell function through production of immunosuppressive cytokines (particularly IL-10 and TGF-β), consumption of IL-2 that is essential for effector T-cell proliferation, and direct contact-dependent suppression through CTLA-4 and other surface molecules.

evidence.quote: There are several Treg cell immune suppressive mechanisms: inhibition of costimulatory signals by CD80 and CD86 expressed by dendritic cells through cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen-4, interleukin (IL)-2 consumption by high-affinity IL-2 receptors with high CD25 (IL-2 receptor α-chain) expression, secretion of inhibitory cytokines
evidence.note: Lists CTLA-4-mediated costimulation inhibition, IL-2 consumption and inhibitory cytokines as Treg suppression mechanisms; IL-10/TGF-beta not named here. Strict re-read: the quote does not state IL-10 and TGF-beta, and direct contact-dependent suppression, not stated in the quote.

evidence.quote: As a key mechanism of Treg-mediated suppression, Treg-expressed CTLA-4 down-regulates the expression of CD80/CD86 costimulatory molecules on antigen-presenting cells (APCs).
evidence.note: Treg CTLA-4 downregulates CD80/CD86 on APCs; contact-dependent but acts via APCs.

claim: Tumor-derived factors including VEGF, IL-10, and PGE2 interfere with DC differentiation and function, preventing effective priming of tumor-specific T cells.

evidence.quote: Tumor-derived prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) impairs antitumor immunity by priming suppressive functions on various immune cell types, including dendritic cells (DCs). In this way, tumors mediate DC dysfunction and hamper their antitumoral activity.
evidence.note: Tumor-derived PGE2 causes DC dysfunction; VEGF and IL-10 effects and T-cell priming not stated.

claim: Tumors also transform nearby blood vessels through production of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), which reduces expression of adhesion molecules on endothelial cells that are essential for T-cell extravasation and infiltration.

evidence.quote: We found that cotreatment with VEGF decreased TNF-α-induced Jurkat cell adhesion to human microvascular endothelial cells by 40%.
evidence.note: VEGF reduces T-cell-line adhesion to endothelial cells in vitro; adhesion molecules not named.

evidence.quote: Inhibition of VEGF signaling in B16 melanoma tumor-bearing mice by sunitinib treatment resulted in up-regulation of CXCL10 and CXCL11 in tumor vessels, accompanied by up to 18-fold increased infiltration of CD3(+) T-lymphocytes in B16 tumors.
evidence.note: Blocking VEGF raises endothelial CXCL10/CXCL11 and T-cell infiltration in mouse tumors; chemokines, not adhesion molecules.

claim: Aberrant glycosylation is particularly common, with tumor-associated glycan structures including truncated O-glycans (such as Tn, sialyl-Tn, and Thomsen-Friedenreich antigens) and altered N-glycosylation patterns.

evidence.quote: An alternative could be the targeting of the tumor glycosylation aberrations, e.g. T/Tn antigens that are truncated O-glycans over-expressed in numerous tumors.
evidence.note: Truncated O-glycans (T/Tn) in tumors; altered N-glycosylation not mentioned.

evidence.quote: Here, we compare mechanisms of aberrant O-glycosylation, i.e., formation of Tn and sialyl-Tn structures, on MUC1 in breast cancer, and on IgA1 in an autoimmune disease, IgA nephropathy.
evidence.note: Tn and sialyl-Tn aberrant O-glycosylation in breast cancer; no N-glycan alterations.

claim: Absence of Central Tolerance: Because neoantigens are not present during thymic T-cell development and negative selection, there is no deletion of high-affinity neoantigen-specific T cells in the thymus.

evidence.quote: Consequently, the protein product in mTECs lacks the immunodominant epitope spanning residues 26-35, thus precluding central tolerance to this antigen.
evidence.note: Thymic epithelium lacks the Melan-A epitope so no central tolerance; a tumor-associated self antigen, not a neoantigen.

evidence.quote: Therefore, hybrid peptide-reactive thymocytes may preferentially escape thymic selection and contribute significantly to T1D progression.
evidence.note: Hybrid peptides absent from thymus let reactive thymocytes escape selection; autoimmune neoantigen, not tumor.

claim: Anti-idiotype vaccines and antibody therapies have been developed to target these antigens, with particular success in B-cell lymphomas where the idiotypic immunoglobulin is abundantly expressed on the cell surface.

evidence.quote: Twelve years after the first formal demonstration that it is possible to vaccinate a cancer patient against an antigen derived from his/her own tumor, idiotype vaccines are now well into Phase III clinical trials for the treatment of follicular lymphoma.
evidence.note: Idiotype vaccines developed and in Phase III trials for follicular lymphoma. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Particular success in B-cell lymphomas and surface idiotype expression not stated; only Phase III follicular lymphoma.

evidence.quote: We conclude that Id-pulsed DC vaccination can induce T-cell and humoral anti-Id immune responses and durable tumor regression.
evidence.note: Idiotype-pulsed vaccination gave immune responses and durable regression in B-cell lymphoma patients. Strict re-read: the quote does not state B-cell lymphoma, anti-idiotype vaccines/antibodies and abundant surface idiotype not stated.

claim: Cancer-testis antigens (CTAs) represent a unique category of proteins expressed in cancer cells and adult reproductive tissues (testis and placenta) but not in other normal adult tissues.

evidence.quote: They are typically expressed in a wide variety of neoplasms and in normal adult tissues are restricted to testicular germ cells.
evidence.note: CT antigens are expressed in many tumors and restricted to testicular germ cells in normal adults; placenta not mentioned.

evidence.quote: HCA587, also known as MAGE-C2, belonging to the MAGE gene family which is characterized by a conserved MAGE Homology Domain, is active in various types of tumors and silent in normal tissues except in male germ-line cells.
evidence.note: One CTA (MAGE-C2) is active in tumors, silent in normal tissues except male germ-line cells; placenta not mentioned.

claim: Evidence from both murine tumor models and human cancer studies has demonstrated that mutations and genetic instability represent the fundamental molecular basis for T-cell-dependent anti-tumor immunity.

evidence.quote: We point out that a fundamental property of the cancer cell, genomic instability, confounds the targeted therapies that aim to induce cell death directly while simultaneously enhancing the potential for immunological attack by creating a large number of neoantigens.
evidence.note: Genomic instability creates neoantigens enhancing immune attack; T-cell dependence not explicitly stated.

evidence.quote: Microsatellite-unstable (MSI) tumours show a high load of mutational neoantigens, as a consequence of DNA mismatch repair deficiency.
evidence.note: Links genetic instability to mutational neoantigens and immune infiltration; T-cell dependence not stated.

claim: Functional melanoma-specific T cells can be propagated from peripheral blood lymphocytes, from tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, or by draining the lymph nodes of patients in whom the melanoma is growing.

evidence.quote: Adoptive T cell therapy (ACT) using ex vivo-expanded autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) can mediate complete regression of certain human cancers.
evidence.note: Shows only tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes as expanded source; blood and lymph node sources not stated.

claim: High Immunogenicity: Novel amino acid sequences in neoantigens are readily recognized as foreign (non-self) by the immune system, much like pathogen-derived antigens.

evidence.quote: Recognized as "non-self" by the immune system, they trigger T-cell responses and enable therapies like personalized vaccines and adoptive T-cell transfer.
evidence.note: Neoantigens recognized as non-self; comparison with pathogen-derived antigens not stated.

evidence.quote: Neoantigens are recognized as non-self and trigger an immune response that is not subject to central and peripheral tolerance.
evidence.note: Recognized as non-self and trigger immune response; no pathogen comparison.

claim: Immune surveillance appears particularly effective against virus-associated tumors, as evidenced by their increased incidence in immunodeficient patients.

evidence.quote: The association between AIDS and a spectrum of malignancies relates to chronic, profound defects in both cellular and humoral mechanisms of immune surveillance.
evidence.note: Links AIDS malignancies to immune surveillance defects; no incidence versus general population and not limited to virus-associated tumors.

claim: In melanoma, tumor-specific antigens were discovered by culturing irradiated tumor cells with autologous lymphocytes, a reaction known as the mixed lymphocyte-tumor cell culture.

evidence.quote: This is the first report on the generation of anti-MAGE CTL by autologous mixed lymphocyte-tumor cell culture (MLTC) from a melanoma patient other than patient MZ2, from whom the first MAGE gene was identified.
evidence.note: Autologous MLTC used to generate anti-MAGE CTL in melanoma; not stated as the original discovery method.

evidence.quote: With one melanoma, the use of autologous CTL clones made it possible to identify 3 different antigens on the tumor cells.
evidence.note: CTL clones from MLTC with irradiated melanoma cells identified melanoma antigens.

claim: In the presence of IFN-γ, the catalytic subunits of standard proteasomes are replaced by alternate subunits to form the immunoproteasome.

evidence.quote: During viral infection, the standard proteasome is replaced by the so-called immunoproteasome (IP) in an IFN-γ-dependent manner.
evidence.note: Standard proteasome is replaced by immunoproteasome in an IFN-gamma-dependent manner; catalytic subunits not named.

evidence.quote: Using transcriptional, proteomic, and functional analyses of proteasomal subunits in inflamed neurons, we found that interferon-γ-mediated induction of the immunoproteasome subunit, proteasome 20S beta 8 (PSMB8) impairs the proteasomal balance, resulting in reduced proteasome activity.
evidence.note: IFN-gamma induces immunoproteasome subunit PSMB8 in neurons; replacement of standard subunits not stated.

claim: Mucin glycoproteins such as MUC1 display altered glycosylation in cancers that exposes normally masked peptide epitopes, creating tumor-associated antigenic determinants.

evidence.quote: Tumor cells tend to overexpress specific mucins, such as the cell surface mucins MUC1 and MUC4 that are engaged in signaling and cell growth, and exhibit abnormal glycosylation.
evidence.note: MUC1 has abnormal glycosylation in tumors; exposure of masked peptide epitopes not stated.

evidence.quote: In this review, we describe three different types of glycoepitopes that are recognized by monoclonal antibodies (mAb) and, therefore, serve as ideal scaffolds for ADC; glycan-only, glycopeptide and shielded-peptide glycoepitopes.
evidence.note: Mentions shielded-peptide glycoepitopes on mucins; does not state that cancer glycosylation exposes masked peptides.

claim: Shared neoantigens arise from recurrent driver mutations that occur in critical oncogenes or tumor suppressor genes (such as KRAS G12D, TP53 R175H, or BRAF V600E mutations) and are expressed by tumors in multiple patients sharing the same mutation.

evidence.quote: In this issue, Kim and colleagues report the first successful application of TCR gene therapy targeting a shared, or public, neoantigen resulting from a TP53 hotspot mutation.
evidence.note: TP53 hotspot driver mutation yields a shared (public) neoantigen. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Recurrent driver mutations as origin of shared neoantigens; KRAS/BRAF examples not stated.

evidence.quote: Since the identified neoantigens might be shared by patients with various types of cancers and are not easily lost due to immune escape, they have the potential to be promising off-the-shelf cancer immunotherapy targets in patients with the corresponding mutations.
evidence.note: Neoantigens from frequent driver mutations (e.g. KRAS-G12D) might be shared among patients; hedged. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Recurrent driver mutations in oncogenes/tumor suppressors and examples not stated; only shared neoantigens as targets.

claim: Similarly, HER2/neu (ERBB2) shows dramatic overexpression in approximately 20-25% of breast cancers, making it a successful therapeutic target.

evidence.quote: Among breast cancer cases, the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer accounts for 15% to 20% and is a crucial focus in the treatment of breast cancer.
evidence.note: States HER2-positive share as 15-20%, a different range than claimed 20-25%.

claim: The MAGE (melanoma-associated antigen) family and NY-ESO-1 are among the most extensively studied CTAs, and their expression across multiple tumor types has made them targets for therapeutic vaccines and adoptive T-cell therapies.

evidence.quote: Afamitresgene autoleucel (afami-cel) is a human leukocyte antigen-restricted autologous T cell therapy targeting melanoma-associated antigen A4 (MAGE-A4), a cancer/testis antigen expressed at varying levels in multiple solid tumors.
evidence.note: MAGE-A4 is expressed in multiple solid tumors and targeted by adoptive T-cell therapy; NY-ESO-1 not covered. Strict re-read: the quote does not state MAGE and NY-ESO-1 as most studied CTAs and vaccines not stated; only MAGE-A4 afami-cel.

evidence.quote: NY-ESO-1, a human cancer-testis antigen, represents an attractive target for such therapies due to its broad expression in different cancer types and the restricted expression in normal tissues.
evidence.note: NY-ESO-1 broadly expressed across cancer types and targeted by T-cell therapies; MAGE not covered. Strict re-read: the quote does not state MAGE family and extensive study; vaccines/adoptive therapy; quote only NY-ESO-1.

claim: The success of prophylactic vaccines against HPV and HBV in preventing virus-associated cancers demonstrates the therapeutic potential of targeting oncoviral antigens.

evidence.quote: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents cervical, head and neck, and anogenital cancers.
evidence.note: States HPV vaccination prevents several cancers; HBV not covered and no vaccinated-vs-unvaccinated incidence given.

claim: B-cell-mediated tumour promotion has been shown to involve different mechanisms, such as production of immunosuppressive cytokines (IL-10) and/or production of antibodies and formation of immune complexes that skew TAMs in an M2-like direction.

evidence.quote: In this issue of the European Journal of Immunology, a study demonstrates that B1 lymphocytes expressing IL-10 play a key role in promoting a pro-tumoral M2-biased phenotype of macrophages.
evidence.note: B cells expressing IL-10 drive M2-biased macrophages; antibody/immune-complex route not stated.

claim: Infiltration of TAMs is generally associated with worse prognosis, which is a reflection of their pro-tumour function.

evidence.quote: The study thus identifies TREM2/APOE/C1Q-positive macrophage infiltration as a potential prognostic biomarker for ccRCC recurrence, as well as a candidate therapeutic target.
evidence.note: Specific macrophage subpopulation infiltration linked to recurrence in ccRCC; not general TAM infiltration.

evidence.quote: CCK8, Transwell invasion, and wound healing further verified that M2 macrophages promoted the proliferation, invasion, and migration of PCa (p < 0.05).
evidence.note: M2 macrophages promote prostate cancer progression; no direct TAM infiltration versus prognosis statement.

claim: Natural killer cells are innate lymphoid cells that have long been considered to play a role in resistance against haematogenous dissemination of cancer cells, in particular to the lungs.

evidence.quote: Its genetic blockade unleashes NK-cell-mediated resistance to hepatic carcinogenesis, haematogenous liver and lung metastasis, and cytomegalovirus infection.
evidence.note: NK cells mediate resistance to haematogenous lung (and liver) metastasis when IL-1R8 is blocked. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Long-held role in resisting dissemination to lungs not stated; only genetic blockade effects.

evidence.quote: Importantly, the reduced lung metastasis of breast cancer by GRh2 was almost abolished upon the depletion of NK cells.
evidence.note: NK cell depletion abolished reduced lung metastasis in mice; supports NK role in limiting lung metastasis.

claim: NK cells have granules with perforins and granzymes that act on target cells inducing lysis or apoptosis and also express PRRs including TLR-2, -3, -4, -5, -7, and -8.

evidence.quote: Mechanistically, lipoteichoic acid (LTA) within SA-EVs engaged Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) on NK cells, activating MyD88/NF-κB signalling pathway.
evidence.note: Shows TLR2 on NK cells only; other TLRs and perforin/granule contents not stated.

evidence.quote: Analysis of GzmA in lymphoid cells following CLP showed that it was mainly expressed by NK cells.
evidence.note: Granzyme A mainly expressed by NK cells; perforin, lysis and TLR repertoire not stated.

claim: AICD is considered to be one of the mechanisms responsible for the increased apoptotic rate among TILs.

evidence.quote: TNF-mediated AICD was also observed upon activation of virus-specific CD8 T cells and tumor-infiltrating CD8 T lymphocytes.
evidence.note: AICD observed in tumor-infiltrating CD8 T cells, via TNF. Strict re-read: the quote does not state AICD as mechanism for increased apoptosis among TILs not stated; only observed in T cells.

evidence.quote: Our data demonstrate that TIL, not tumor, express both Fas and FasL, are arrested in G(1), do not secrete cytokine in situ, and, upon activation in vitro and in vivo, rapidly die by activation-induced cell death.
evidence.note: TIL die by AICD upon activation but are not apoptotic in situ; contribution to in situ apoptosis not shown.

claim: Dysfunctional immune responses can result as some tumor cells express Fas ligand (FasL) and bind Fas expressed on some infiltrating lymphocytes resulting in AICD seems to be differentially regulated in T-helper subsets.

evidence.quote: Recent evidence indicates that other cells in the tumor microenvironment can express FasL and trigger apoptosis of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL), including endothelial cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells.
evidence.note: FasL on microenvironment cells (endothelial, MDSC, not tumor cells) kills TIL, impairing anti-tumor immunity.

evidence.quote: Moreover, FasL is discussed as direct effector molecule for the establishment of immune privilege and tumour survival.
evidence.note: FasL linked to immune privilege and tumour survival; tumor-cell FasL killing lymphocytes not stated.

claim: Over the past decade, a number of reports have provided data indicating that tumor cells can either directly produce PGs or induce macrophages in the tumor microenvironment to secrete PGs.

evidence.quote: These immunosuppressive events are mediated by tumor cell derived fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) and prostaglandin E2 (PGE2).
evidence.note: Tumor cells are a source of PGE2 in the microenvironment. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Tumor cells or macrophages producing prostaglandins; quote only FGF2/PGE2 mediate immunosuppression.

evidence.quote: Transcriptomic analysis revealed elevated COX1/2 expression in TAMs in MSS tumors compared with MSI tumors.
evidence.note: Tumor-associated macrophages express COX1/2 and drive PGE2 signalling; macrophage induction by tumor cells not stated.

claim: Overexpression of COX-2 results in increased production of PGs by tumor cells and, in the case of PGE2, results in an upregulation of antiapoptotic proteins, such as Bcl-2, in tumor cells.

evidence.quote: Additionally, PGE2 inhibits programmed cell death caused by SC-58125 and induces Bcl-2 expression, but did not affect Bcl-x or Bax expression in human colon cancer (HCA-7) cells.
evidence.note: PGE2 induces Bcl-2 in COX-2-expressing colon cancer cells; COX-2 raising PG production not directly stated.

evidence.quote: In addition, PTGS2 mediated cisplatin-induced BCL2 expression and subsequent resistance to apoptosis via PGE2/EP4/MAPKs (ERK1/2, P38) axis.
evidence.note: PTGS2 (COX-2) drives BCL2 expression via PGE2/EP4 in gastric cancer cells.

claim: Rapidly growing tumor cells require nutrients, oxygen, and essential metabolites to proliferate and, at the same time, create an immunosuppressive microenvironment.

evidence.quote: Therapeutics that target metabolic restrictions, such as low glucose levels, a low pH, hypoxia and the generation of suppressive metabolites, have shown promise as combination therapies for different types of cancer.
evidence.note: Tumour microenvironment metabolic restrictions (low glucose, hypoxia) limit antitumour T cells; tumor consumption not stated.

evidence.quote: Initial research has uncovered immunosuppressive properties of the TME, which include low oxygen levels (hypoxia), acidic conditions (low pH), increased interstitial pressure, heightened permeability of tumor vasculature, and an inflammatory microenvironment.
evidence.note: Hypoxia and acidity listed as immunosuppressive TME features; link to tumor consumption not stated.

claim: The pathway responsible for these effects has recently been elucidated as being a consequence of cyclooxygenase (COX) overexpression in cancer cells, particularly COX-2.

evidence.quote: In vivo CRISPR-Cas9 screening in an immunogenic murine lung cancer model identified mechanisms by which oncogenic KRAS promotes immune evasion, most notably via upregulation of immunosuppressive COX2 in cancer cells.
evidence.note: COX2 upregulation in cancer cells drives immune evasion in KRAS-mutant lung cancer. Strict re-read: the quote does not state No statement that COX overexpression explains the effects; only KRAS-driven COX2 in murine lung cancer.

evidence.quote: Notably, tumor production of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) leads to evasion of the NK cell-cDC1 axis in part by impairing NK cell viability and chemokine production, as well as by causing downregulation of chemokine receptor expression in cDC1.
evidence.note: Tumor-produced PGE2 mediates immune evasion; COX-2 overexpression not named.

claim: The tumor microenvironment physically constitutes a barrier against T-cell infiltration, as it is a compact structure with tight interactions among cancer cells, fibroblasts, immune cells, and ECM.

evidence.quote: We find that tumor cells and secreted phosphoprotein 1-positive macrophages interact with collagen type XI alpha 1 chain-positive cancer-associated fibroblasts to stimulate the deposition and entanglement of collagen fibers at tumor boundaries, obstructing T cell infiltration and leading to poor prognosis.
evidence.note: Cell interactions build collagen barrier at tumor boundaries obstructing T cell infiltration. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Compact TME with tight interactions among cells and ECM as physical barrier not stated.

evidence.quote: This interaction might be regulated by chemerin, TGF-β, and interleukin-1, which would stimulate the formation of immune-excluded desmoplasic structure and limit the T cell infiltration.
evidence.note: Fibroblast-macrophage interaction forms immune-excluded desmoplastic structure limiting T cell infiltration. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Physical barrier from compact structure not stated; only 'might be regulated' immune exclusion.

claim: There is ample evidence that tumor cells produce immunosuppressive factors, and this has been verified to have local as well as systemic effects on immune function.

evidence.quote: Exosomal PD-L1 from the tumor suppresses T cell activation in the draining lymph node. Systemically introduced exosomal PD-L1 rescues growth of tumors unable to secrete their own.
evidence.note: Tumor-derived exosomal PD-L1 suppresses T cells locally (draining node) and acts systemically. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Only exosomal PD-L1; general production of immunosuppressive factors by tumor cells not stated.

evidence.quote: Notably, IL-35 is produced by regulatory T cells and breast cancer cells.
evidence.note: Breast cancer cells produce immunosuppressive IL-35; local/systemic action not specified.

claim: Acquired resistance develops through various mechanisms including loss of target antigens, evolution of less immunogenic tumor clones, and upregulation of alternative immune checkpoints.

evidence.quote: Throughout these phases, tumour immunogenicity is edited, and immunosuppressive mechanisms that enable disease progression are acquired. The mechanisms of resistance to immunotherapy seem to broadly overlap with those used by cancers as they undergo immunoediting to evade detection by the immune system.
evidence.note: Immunogenicity editing overlaps resistance mechanisms; antigen loss and alternative checkpoints not named.

claim: CAR T cells combined with checkpoint blockade (particularly anti-PD-1) represent a rational combination, as checkpoint inhibitors can counteract the exhaustion that CAR T cells undergo within the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.

evidence.quote: Anti-PD-1 therapy can possibly reverse CAR T cells exhaustion in DLBCL.
evidence.note: Title states anti-PD-1 can possibly reverse CAR T exhaustion in DLBCL; hedged, no abstract. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Combination with CAR T generally, anti-PD-1 reversal certain; only DLBCL 'possibly'.

evidence.quote: The TME sets major obstacles for CAR-T therapies, creating conditions that suppress the immune response, inducing T cell exhaustion. To enhance treatment efficacy, specific efforts associated with CAR-T cell therapy in NSCLC, should definitely focus TME-related immunosuppression and antigen escape mechanisms, by combining CAR-T cells with immune checkpoint blockades.
evidence.note: TME induces CAR-T exhaustion; combining CAR-T with checkpoint blockade proposed (not anti-PD-1 specifically). Strict re-read: the quote does not state Anti-PD-1 specifically and checkpoint inhibitors counteracting exhaustion not stated; only NSCLC.

claim: Clinical trials combining CAR T cells targeting mesothelin, EGFRvIII, or other solid tumor antigens with pembrolizumab or other checkpoint inhibitors are ongoing in glioblastoma, mesothelioma, and other solid tumors.

evidence.quote: Phase 2 part of the study, the investigators will test the dose in combination with another drug, pembrolizumab, to see what effects the study treatment has on malignant pleural mesothelioma.
evidence.note: Mesothelin CAR T plus pembrolizumab in mesothelioma; status active, not recruiting (ongoing). Strict re-read: the quote does not state Mesothelin, EGFRvIII CAR T combinations; glioblastoma; quote only pembrolizumab in mesothelioma trial.

evidence.quote: This is an open-label, phase 1 study to assess the safety and tolerability of EGFRvIII T cells in combination with pembrolizumab (PD-1 Inhibitor) in patients with newly diagnosed, EGFRvIII+, MGMT-unmethylated glioblastoma.
evidence.note: dated: EGFRvIII CAR T plus pembrolizumab in glioblastoma; record status now COMPLETED, not ongoing.

claim: Mechanisms of primary resistance include lack of neoantigen expression, defects in antigen presentation machinery, absence of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, and intrinsic immunosuppression within the tumor microenvironment.

evidence.quote: Hot tumors, characterized by heightened immune activity and responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), stand in stark contrast to cold tumors, which lack immune infiltration and remain resistant to therapy.
evidence.note: Covers lack of immune infiltration as resistance; does not list the other mechanisms.

evidence.quote: The last decade has witnessed unprecedented succusses with the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors in treating cancer. Nevertheless, the proportion of patients who respond favorably to the treatment remained rather modest, partially due to treatment resistance.
evidence.note: Notes primary and acquired resistance exist but does not list the mechanisms.

claim: Novel immune checkpoint targets beyond PD-1 and CTLA-4—including LAG-3, TIM-3, TIGIT, and VISTA—are being evaluated in clinical trials, either as monotherapies or in combination with established checkpoint inhibitors, with the goal of overcoming resistance mechanisms.

evidence.quote: This is a multicentre, phase IIR, double non-comparative arm trial, with an initial safety run for the anti-LAG3 arm.
evidence.note: one instance: recruiting trial with an anti-LAG3 arm; the combination with cemiplimab is in the title. Strict re-read: the quote does not state LAG-3 only; TIM-3, TIGIT, VISTA, monotherapy/combination, overcoming resistance not stated.

evidence.quote: An Exploratory, Open-label, Multicenter Phase 1b Trial to Evaluate Safety and Efficacy of Sym021 (Anti-PD 1) in Combination With Either Sym022 (Anti-LAG-3) or Sym023 (Anti-TIM-3) or Sym023 and Irinotecan
evidence.note: dated: one instance: anti-PD-1 plus anti-LAG-3 or anti-TIM-3 trial, now COMPLETED, started 2020.

claim: Oncolytic viruses, which selectively infect and lyse tumor cells while releasing tumor antigens and damage-associated molecular patterns, can convert "cold" non-inflamed tumors into "hot" inflamed tumors that become responsive to checkpoint inhibitors.

evidence.quote: Tumors with a low level of pre-existing immune cell infiltration respond poorly to immune checkpoint therapies. Oncolytic viruses optimize immunotherapies by modulating the tumor microenvironment and affecting multiple steps in the cancer-immunity cycle, making them an attractive agent for combination strategies.
evidence.note: Oncolytic viruses modulate the microenvironment of poorly infiltrated tumors to improve checkpoint therapy. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Selective infection/lysis, antigen release, and converting cold to hot tumors not stated.

evidence.quote: This editorial proposes that the TGF-β trap of AdAPT-001 reverses the immunosuppressive environment of tumor cells, and thus makes these tumors susceptible to CIs like the anti-PD-1 agent, nivolumab, and potentially other therapies as well.
evidence.note: An oncolytic adenovirus is proposed to make tumors susceptible to checkpoint inhibitors. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Selective infection/lysis, antigen release, and cold-to-hot conversion by oncolytic viruses generally not stated.

claim: PD-L1 expression on tumor cells, tumor mutational burden (TMB), microsatellite instability, deficient mismatch repair, and inflammatory gene expression signatures all serve as predictive biomarkers for checkpoint inhibitor response, although none are perfectly predictive.

evidence.quote: Biomarkers such as PD-L1 expression, tumor mutational burden (TMB), and Human Papillomavirus (HPV) status play a critical role in treatment selection, but further validation is needed.
evidence.note: PD-L1 and TMB are treatment-selection biomarkers needing further validation; MSI, dMMR, signatures not covered.

evidence.quote: High-frequency MSI (MSI-H)/dMMR is gaining increasing interest as a biomarker for advanced cancer patients to determine their eligibility for immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs).
evidence.note: MSI-H/dMMR described as a biomarker for checkpoint inhibitor eligibility; predictive performance not given.

claim: Personalized neoantigen vaccines require complex manufacturing workflows, face challenges in accurately predicting immunogenic neoantigens (high false-positive rates in computational predictions), and must overcome tumor heterogeneity where not all cancer cells express the targeted neoantigens.

evidence.quote: Despite the promise of AI-powered cancer vaccines, significant challenges remain, such as tumor heterogeneity and genetic variability, which can limit the effectiveness of neoantigen prediction.
evidence.note: Names heterogeneity and prediction limits as challenges; manufacturing complexity not mentioned.

evidence.quote: In this Review, we focus on the key obstacles pertaining to vaccine design and tumour environment that remain to be overcome in order to unleash the true potential of neoantigen vaccines in cancer therapy.
evidence.note: Reviews obstacles to personalized neoantigen vaccines without listing manufacturing, prediction or heterogeneity.

claim: Preclinical studies have demonstrated that PD-1 inhibition combined with CAR T cells results in decreased myeloid-derived suppressor cell accumulation in tumors, reduced CAR T-cell exhaustion, and enhanced anti-tumor efficacy.

evidence.quote: Anti-PD-1 therapy can possibly reverse CAR T cells exhaustion in DLBCL.
evidence.note: Anti-PD-1 reversing CAR T exhaustion (hedged); MDSC accumulation and efficacy not stated.

evidence.quote: Additionally, human IL-18-secreting anti-DLL3 CAR T cells showed an increased memory phenotype, less exhaustion, and induced durable responses in multiple SCLC models, an effect that could be further enhanced with anti-PD-1 blockade.
evidence.note: IL-18 CAR T cells less exhausted, effect enhanced by anti-PD-1; MDSC not mentioned.

claim: Predicted neoantigens are prioritized based on multiple factors including mutation expression level, predicted MHC binding affinity, peptide processing probability, and foreignness relative to normal sequences.

evidence.quote: Prioritization of predicted peptides occurs by integrating diverse data, including mutant allele expression, peptide binding affinities, and determination whether a mutation is clonal or subclonal.
evidence.note: Lists expression and binding affinity plus clonality; no peptide processing or foreignness.

evidence.quote: We propose four peptide novelty metrics to refine predicted neoantigenicity: tumor vs. paired normal peptide binding affinity difference, tumor vs. paired normal peptide sequence similarity, tumor vs. closest human peptide sequence similarity, and tumor vs. closest microbial peptide sequence similarity.
evidence.note: Novelty (difference from normal) metrics correspond to foreignness; other listed criteria differ.

claim: Selected neoantigens are then synthesized as peptides, encoded in mRNA or DNA vectors, or loaded onto autologous dendritic cells for patient vaccination, often in combination with adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity.

evidence.quote: Recent advancements in vaccine platforms, such as synthetic peptides, mRNA, DNA, cellular, and nano-vaccines, have enhanced antigen presentation and immune activation.
evidence.note: Lists peptide, mRNA, DNA and cellular platforms; not specifically autologous dendritic cell vaccines or neoantigen formulation.
